author.agent: root author review of pre-existing content

corrections: pipe-iron-law.questions.json: Correct percentage-product comparison; remove unsupported historical anecdote.
pipe-iron-law.questions.json: Do not imply a verified historical product comparison.
pipe-iron-law.questions.json: Dynamic count must be fixed, not executable size.
pipe-iron-law.questions.json: Average IPC does not describe every cycle.
pipe-iron-law.questions.json: Largest original share is not universal optimisation rule.
pipe-iron-law.questions.json: A hotter cache usually means more hits, not more pressure.
pipe-five-stage.md: Scope timing conclusion to worked design.
pipe-five-stage.md: Pipelining does not mathematically require strictly greater latency.
pipe-five-stage.md: Avoid universal assertion across ISA families and extensions.
pipe-five-stage.md: Not every format of every named ISA keeps every field fixed.
pipe-five-stage.md: Distinguish data model from all memory accesses.
pipe-five-stage.md: Avoid universal latency claim.
pipe-five-stage.questions.json: Predecode may establish lengths without complete decode.
pipe-five-stage.questions.json: Stage splitting is not the only possible implementation change.
pipe-five-stage.questions.json: Exact fill/drain calculation needs model assumptions.
pipe-hazards.md: Do not generalise one trace to all workloads.
pipe-hazards.questions.json: Avoid double-counting hidden overlapping costs.
pipe-branch-prediction.md: Scope BTB timing to model.
pipe-branch-prediction.questions.json: Source-language structure does not fix branch direction.
pipe-branch-prediction.questions.json: Do not claim identical hardware cache behaviour from identical addresses alone.
pipe-branch-prediction.questions.json: Scope implementation-specific lookup timing.
pipe-branch-prediction.questions.json: No universal BTB timing.
pipe-branch-prediction.questions.json: Worked explanation had labelled a correct definition false.
pipe-branch-prediction.questions.json: The unconditional +=0 adds observable accesses for volatile/atomic objects.
pipe-branch-prediction.questions.json: Restrict semantic equivalence to supplied plain-object contract.
pipe-out-of-order.md: Average throughput does not require multiple starts every cycle.
pipe-out-of-order.md: Renaming does not remove all non-register constraints.
pipe-out-of-order.questions.json: ROB is one precise-state mechanism, not necessary to every possible OoO design.
pipe-out-of-order.questions.json: Precise retirement is not interthread memory consistency.
pipe-out-of-order.questions.json: Remove ambiguous historical retrofit implication.
pipe-out-of-order.questions.json: ROB allocation capacity is not complete latency hiding.
pipe-out-of-order.questions.json: Reclamation must account for in-flight writes and outstanding users.
pipe-out-of-order.questions.json: Do not imply unsafe immediate physical-register recycling.
pipe-out-of-order.questions.json: Conflicting access does not prove values differ.
pipe-power-wall.md: Avoid unqualified historical leakage growth across all process generations.
pipe-power-wall.md: Race to idle need not or generally does not shut system down entirely.
pipe-power-wall.questions.json: Avoid false either/or history from hypothetical arithmetic.
pipe-power-wall.questions.json: Breakdown of ideal model is not a universal stop in per-transistor power reduction.

retrofit: glossary ibm-360-91: alias 'System/360' (the whole family) mapped to the Model 91; removed. turbo-boost: alias 'base frequency' removed.
retrofit: glossary stage-if, supply-voltage, reorder-buffer: definitions generalised/scoped because their aliases fall back into OS, security, synth and networking lessons with a broader sense.

retrofit: glossary cache-miss-arch ('hundreds of cycles' scoped to misses to main memory), return-address-stack (overflow wording), dennard-scaling (hedged date, 'result' not 'observation'), perceptron-predictor (now defines a perceptron), instructions-per-cycle (removed 'usually above 1 in their ideal case').

retrofit: glossary sources: broken Wikipedia anchors fixed (Hazard #Read_after_write_(RAW)/#Write_after_read_(WAR)/#Write_after_write_(WAW) -> #Data_hazards; Branch_predictor #Two-bit_saturating_counter -> #Saturating_counter; Exception_handling #Exception_handling_in_hardware -> #Hardware_exceptions).

retrofit: glossary: 'misprediction rate' split into its own entry (branch-misprediction is shadowed by Arch 03); perf-tool turned into a 'perf stat' entry (term 'perf' owned by Arch 03); dead aliases 'write-back' (stage-wb) and '2-bit counter' (saturating-counter) removed.

lowConfidence.claim: return-address-stack: behaviour when a call chain is deeper than the stack
lowConfidence.reason: Overwrite/loss of oldest entries is the usual circular-buffer design, but overflow handling is implementation-specific; wording hedged ('may then be mispredicted').

lowConfidence.claim: cache-miss-arch: a miss to main memory can cost hundreds of cycles on a fast core
lowConfidence.reason: Consistent with the lesson's own 80 ns at 4 GHz = 320 cycles example; real latencies are product-specific.

lowConfidence.claim: Supply voltage 'of the order of 1 V' in a modern processor core
lowConfidence.reason: Hedged order-of-magnitude statement; no product datasheet fetched. Arch 02's VDD entry gives 0.6 to 1.2 V.
